Hyperacausality removes the cause of the acausality.","class":"Meta-order acausality","commonly_confused_with":"Standard first-order acausality.","formal_logic":"¬∃c: c => (¬∃k: k => S)","id":"hyperacausality","name":"Hyperacausality","sources":["site/sources/zubaida/1a0601fc96f7add3.txt","causal-ontology.json"]}

full_text:
{"canon_definition":"An update implemented across the fundamental structures of reality where if the reason why a cause is not a rewrite would itself be a rewrite, that reason is conceptually rewritten so that it was never a rewrite, applying recursively across every explanatory order without terminal depth.","clarification":"Produces absolute rewrite-originlessness. The resulting effect X remains real and permanent, while no causal, reasonal, metacausal, metareasonal, or recursively higher explanatory path can truthfully terminate in or derive its rewrite status from a rewrite.","class":"Infinite-depth explanatory erasure","commonly_confused_with":"Mere memory wiping or simple timeline branching.","formal_logic":"∀ e ∈ ExplanatoryOrders: ¬RewriteGround(e, X) ∧ X = Persist","historical_clarification":"Negative Rewrite removes its own surviving causal provenance. Hypernegative Rewrite recursively blocks every higher explanation that would restore rewrite-provenance. It produces rewrite-originlessness, not mere hidden causation.","historical_formal":["Y Γƒ╢ X","P Γƒ╢ ┬¼RewriteOrigin(Y, X) Γêº ┬¼RewriteOrigin(P, X)","X persists","ΓêÇ explanatory orders e: ┬¼RewriteGround(e, X)"],"historical_summary":"An effect-producing rewrite whose rewrite-origin is recursively excluded at every causal, reasonal, and mixed explanatory order while the effect remains real.","id":"hypernegative-rewrite","name":"Hypernegative Rewrite","sources":["site/sources/zubaida/1a0601fc96f7add3.txt","causal-ontology.json"],"summary":"An effect-producing rewrite whose rewrite-origin is recursively excluded at every causal, reasonal, and mixed explanatory order while the effect remains real.","title":"Hypernegative Rewrite","verbatim_canon_source_history":["Hypernegative Rewrite is a rewrite in which an initial rewrite Y produces an effect X, after which another rewrite P conceptually erases both Y and P from ever qualifying as the rewrite-origin of X at any explanatory order.","This conceptual erasure applies not only to the direct cause of X, but recursively to every cause, reason, cause-for-reason, reason-for-cause, metacause, metareason, metacausal-reason, metareasonal-cause, and every recursively higher or mixed causal-reasonal relation through which the existence or state of X could ultimately be attributed to a rewrite.","Thus, even if the direct cause of X is rewritten so that it was never itself a rewrite, Hypernegative Rewrite does not stop there. If the reason why that cause is not a rewrite would itself be a rewrite, that reason is also conceptually rewritten so that it was never a rewrite. The same operation applies recursively to the cause of that reason, the reason for that cause, the cause of the reason for that cause, and every further explanatory order without terminal depth.","The resulting effect X remains real, while no causal, reasonal, metacausal, metareasonal, causal-reasonal, reasonal-causal, or recursively higher explanatory path can truthfully terminate in, depend upon, or derive its rewrite-status from a rewrite."],"verbatim_source_canon":"Hypernegative Rewrite is a rewrite in which an initial rewrite Y produces an effect X, after which another rewrite P conceptually erases both Y and P from ever qualifying as the rewrite-origin of X at any explanatory order.

This conceptual erasure applies not only to the direct cause of X, but recursively to every cause, reason, cause-for-reason, reason-for-cause, metacause, metareason, metacausal-reason, metareasonal-cause, and every recursively higher or mixed causal-reasonal relation through which the existence or state of X could ultimately be attributed to a rewrite.

Thus, even if the direct cause of X is rewritten so that it was never itself a rewrite, Hypernegative Rewrite does not stop there. If the reason why that cause is not a rewrite would itself be a rewrite, that reason is also conceptually rewritten so that it was never a rewrite. The same operation applies recursively to the cause of that reason, the reason for that cause, the cause of the reason for that cause, and every further explanatory order without terminal depth.

The resulting effect X remains real, while no causal, reasonal, metacausal, metareasonal, causal-reasonal, reasonal-causal, or recursively higher explanatory path can truthfully terminate in, depend upon, or derive its rewrite-status from a rewrite."}
title: Hypernegative Rewrite

full_text: {"canon_definition":"Infracausality is the acausality of the causality of something. An infracause is the foundational non-contingent root underlying a causal mechanism.","clarification":"Where causality operates as a function, infracausality denotes that the function itself operates without causal antecedents.","class":"Sub-causal mechanics","commonly_confused_with":"Supracausality.","formal_logic":"Infracausality(S) = Acausality(Causality(S))","id":"infracausality","name":"Infracausality & Infracause","sources":["site/sources/zubaida/19ef0e52f69e4ad4.txt"]}

full_text: {"canon_definition":"Lifras are necessitative causes for anything that the observer perceives as cognitive errors, mistakes, or suboptimalities.","clarification":"Under Empress Rhayhara's reign, all Lifras are Hypernegatively Rewritten so they have never existed across any order of her parahistorical being.","class":"Necessitative imperfection factor","commonly_confused_with":"Psychological flaws or random bad luck.","formal_logic":"Lifra(L) => Error(E); HypernegativeRewrite(¬∃L) => ¬∃E","id":"lifra","name":"Lifra & Error-Cause Mechanics","sources":["site/sources/zubaida/1a0601fc96f7add3.txt"]}

full_text: {"canon_definition":"The formal causal mechanics where the ontological invariance of an effect (E) retrocausally forces the negation of any potential cause (¬C) that would prevent E, and necessitates the existence of any prerequisite (P) required for E.","clarification":"Based on classical Modus Tollens (P => Q ⊢ ¬Q => ¬P). If Imperial victory is invariant (V = TRUE), then any attack A that entails ¬V is rendered counterfactually impossible and neutralized at the root.","class":"Contrapositive causal necessity","commonly_confused_with":"Conventional fate or destiny (Modus-Tollens causality is active ontological enforcement, not passive prophecy).","formal_logic":"(C => ¬Invariant) ∧ Invariant => ¬C","id":"modus-tollens-causality","name":"Modus-Tollens Causalities","sources":["Hypergendered Logic","causal-ontology.json"]}

full_text: {"canon_definition":"An operation where a state or timeline is rewritten, and the rewrite itself retroactively removes its own surviving causal provenance so that it was never caused as a rewrite.","clarification":"Unlike standard timeline alterations that leave an active rewritelog or paradox trace, Negative Rewrite erases the fact that an alteration occurred. full_text: {"canon_definition":"A state that entirely transcends the conceptually allowable limits of the concepts of causality, acausality, metacausality, metaacausality, supracausality, and infracausality.","clarification":"Simulated and stress-tested by Clan Varvadeil against high-tier conceptual threats. Renders conceptual erasure and acausality-negation attacks structurally irrelevant.","class":"Meta-ontological state","commonly_confused_with":"Mere immunity to magic.","formal_logic":"Outercausal(S) => S ∉ (Causality ∪ Acausality ∪ Supracausality ∪ Infracausality)","id":"outercausality-stage-1","name":"Outercausality Stage 1","sources":["site/sources/zubaida/19ef0e52f69e4ad4.txt"]}

{"canon_definition":"The total causal-derivational structure of rewrites affecting a subject or domain, including every rewrite of any kind and every higher-order rewrite causally responsible for producing, modifying, replacing, retrocausing, beginninglessifying, or determining another rewrite.","clarification":"Parahistory is a multi-dimensional directed acyclic graph (or hypergraph) of rewrites. A beginningless history can itself possess a higher-order parahistorical cause that caused that history to have never had a beginning.","class":"Rewrite-derivational network","commonly_confused_with":"Linear timeline or historical chronicle.","formal_logic":"Parahistory(S) = { (R_i, R_j) | R_i causally produces or alters R_j on domain S }","historical_clarification":"This nonlinearly generalized definition is ontologically stronger and more precise than the earlier draft describing only timelines arranged from earlier cause to later effect.","historical_formal":["Parahistory(subject) = total rewrite-causal derivation graph affecting subject","Sequence Γèé Parahistory; Parahistory Γëá merely sequence"],"historical_summary":"The total causal-derivational structure of rewrites affecting a subject or domain, including rewrites of histories, ordering relations, and whole rewrite-structures.","id":"parahistory","name":"Parahistory","sources":["site/sources/zubaida/19e56867bf1bf3d3.txt","site/sources/zubaida/1a0601fc96f7add3.txt"],"summary":"The total causal-derivational structure of rewrites affecting a subject or domain, including rewrites of histories, ordering relations, and whole rewrite-structures.","title":"Parahistory","verbatim_canon_source_history":["Parahistory is the total causal-derivational structure of rewrites affecting a subject or domain, including every rewrite of any kind and every higher-order rewrite causally responsible for producing, modifying, replacing, retrocausing, beginninglessifying, or otherwise determining another rewrite or rewrite-structure.","Parahistory is not restricted to a single temporal sequence. It includes rewrite-chains, branching rewrite-networks, rewritten rewrite-chains, rewrites of the ordering relations between rewrites, and higher-order rewrites that generate or alter entire rewrite-structures.","A later parahistorical state therefore need not simply occur after an earlier one. It may exist because an earlier-order rewrite caused that state, its history, its causal ordering, or even its apparent beginninglessness to obtain.","Thus a beginningless rewrite-history may itself possess a higher-order parahistorical cause: a rewrite that caused that history to have never had a beginning."],"verbatim_source_canon":"Parahistory is the total causal-derivational structure of rewrites affecting a subject or domain, including every rewrite of any kind and every higher-order rewrite causally responsible for producing, modifying, replacing, retrocausing, beginninglessifying, or otherwise determining another rewrite or rewrite-structure.

Parahistory is not restricted to a single temporal sequence. It includes rewrite-chains, branching rewrite-networks, rewritten rewrite-chains, rewrites of the ordering relations between rewrites, and higher-order rewrites that generate or alter entire rewrite-structures.

A later parahistorical state therefore need not simply occur after an earlier one. It may exist because an earlier-order rewrite caused that state, its history, its causal ordering, or even its apparent beginninglessness to obtain.

Thus a beginningless rewrite-history may itself possess a higher-order parahistorical cause: a rewrite that caused that history to have never had a beginning."}
title: Parahistory

full_text: {"canon_definition":"A state in which something's acausality possesses no cause, reason, ground, origin, prerequisite, or derivational basis, and this nonderivation holds recursively at every higher causal and explanatory order without terminal depth.","clarification":"The absolute peak of causal independence in the Arthitean Codex. Closes all meta-theoretical regresses across causality, metacausality, reasonal logic, and parahistorical derivation.","class":"Supreme nonderivation operator","commonly_confused_with":"Simple omnipotence or ungrounded existence.","formal_logic":"∀ n ≥ 0: Nonderivation(Order_n(S)) ∧ ¬∃Reason(Order_n(S))","historical_clarification":"Of the proposed precedence formulations, this is the strongest because it closes the higher-order explanatory regress. Beginninglessness removes a first temporal member; acausality removes an origin-cause; hyperacausality removes a cause of that acausality; Transrecursive Hypercausality extends that nonderivation through every causal, reasonal, and mixed metaorder.","historical_formal":["NΓéÇ = nonderivation(subject)","ΓêÇn ΓëÑ 0: NΓéÖ has neither cause nor reason, and NΓéÖΓéèΓéü = nonderivation(NΓéÖ)"],"historical_summary":"Acausality and its explanatory nongrounding hold at every recursively higher causal and reasonal order.","id":"transrecursive-hypercausality","name":"Transrecursive Hypercausality","sources":["site/sources/zubaida/1a0601fc96f7add3.txt","causal-ontology.json"],"summary":"Acausality and its explanatory nongrounding hold at every recursively higher causal and reasonal order.","title":"Transrecursive Hypercausality","verbatim_canon_source_history":["Transrecursive Hypercausality is a state in which something's acausality possesses no cause, reason, ground, origin, prerequisite, or derivational basis, and this nonderivation holds recursively at every higher causal and explanatory order, with each order lacking a cause and lacking a reason.","This necessarily entails that something which is Transrecursively Hypercausal is acausal and hyperacausal; has no reason for its acausality and hyperacausality; and has a lack of reason that is itself acausal and hyperacausal at every recursive level."],"verbatim_source_canon":"Transrecursive Hypercausality is a state in which something's acausality possesses no cause, reason, ground, origin, prerequisite, or derivational basis, and this nonderivation holds recursively at every higher causal and explanatory order, with each order lacking a cause and lacking a reason.\n\nThis necessarily entails that something which is Transrecursively Hypercausal is acausal and hyperacausal; has no reason for its acausality and hyperacausality; and has a lack of reason that is itself acausal and hyperacausal at every recursive level."}
